correctness.rationale: Each color class must be independent and have zero or odd intersection with every open neighborhood; these classwise tests jointly suffice. A class spanning both shores must be a deleted pair, since all other cross-shore pairs are edges. A side-only class of size r with 2≤r<n produces positive counts r and r−1 at opposite vertices of the missing matching, which cannot both be odd. A whole shore contributes n−1 to every opposite vertex and is allowed exactly when n is even; singletons and deleted pairs always work. A partition without either whole shore chooses s of the n matching pairs and uses 2n−s names, giving the first falling-factorial sum. For even n there are also two partitions with one whole shore and opposite singletons, and one partition with both whole shores. These give precisely the correction terms. The least color counts are n and 2 in the respective parity cases; the palette formula includes q=0 with all terms zero. Independent definition tests checked 349,497 candidate classes for n=3–9 and 120,318 full partitions for n=3–5, agreeing with the class list and all falling-factorial coefficients tested.
residual_risks: Finite tests check candidate-class admissibility through n=9 and all partition coefficients through n=5, not unrestricted n. Color-name injections and the class proof establish the palette polynomial at all q≥0.

originality.rationale: Theorem 4.4 of Caro et al. explicitly gives both parity branches of the scalar. More decisively, the argument for claim (v) in its proof excludes every proper nontrivial sub-row or sub-column color class by the positive counts r−1 and r, irrespective of the full row or column size's parity. Only its full-row case uses odd order. Specializing that argument to K_n×K_2 gives the complete class list even for even n. Counting disjoint whole columns and the three possible whole-shore partitions is then direct, so the new wording and displayed polynomial do not establish a distinct exact fact. This judgment is based on the available proof, not a claim that the earlier theorem statement prints the polynomial.
residual_risks: The focused public search was uninformative and does not establish absence of other sources. The negative decision rests on the positive proof-level implication, not a date-based priority inference or a claim about uninspected sources.

The minimum is explicitly known and the full count here is routine bookkeeping after that proof, with no independently useful unknown exact fact left by narrowing to the even case.
residual_risks: This assessment is confined to the frozen crown enumerator, not to other strong-odd counting questions on graph products.
